q: Genetic code is a set of rules for determining how genetic information is converted to an _____ sequence of a protein.
e: Genetic code is a set of rules for determining how genetic information is converted to an amino acid sequence of a protein. So we write amino acid. Leave nucleotide and fatty acid out.

q: The genetic code defines a code specifying the relationship between a nucleotide codon and an _____.
e: The genetic code defines a code specifying the relationship between a nucleotide codon and an nucleotide. The blank is nucleotide. Not amino acid or polypeptide.

q: Researchers knew that there are only four nucleotides in RNA, but _____ different kinds of amino acids.
e: Researchers knew that there are only four nucleotides in RNA, but 20 different kinds of amino acids. The blank is 20. Not 10 or 15.

q: The minimum combination of the four nucleotides was a triplet code, which could produce _____ possible combinations.
e: The minimum combination of the four nucleotides was a triplet code, which could produce 64 possible combinations. So we write 64. Leave 32 and 16 out.

q: The triplet hypothesis proposed that the genetic code consists of a combination of three nucleotides, called a _____.
e: The triplet hypothesis proposed that the genetic code consists of a combination of three nucleotides, called a codon. Codon is the word, not anticodon or promoter.

q: Between 1961 and 1965, various research groups compared artificially synthesized RNA molecules with the amino acid sequences of _____.
e: Between 1961 and 1965, various research groups compared artificially synthesized RNA molecules with the amino acid sequences of polypeptides. The blank is polypeptides. Not nucleotides or DNA.

q: By convention, the genetic code is always interpreted in terms of the _____ codon rather than the DNA sequence.
e: By convention, the genetic code is always interpreted in terms of the mRNA codon rather than the DNA sequence. MRNA is the word, not tRNA or rRNA.

q: The genetic code is _____, meaning that more than one codon can code for the same amino acid.
e: The genetic code is redundant, meaning that more than one codon can code for the same amino acid. Redundant is the word, not continuous or universal.

q: There are only _____ codons that do not code for any amino acid and serve as stop signals.
e: There are only three codons that do not code for any amino acid and serve as stop signals. Three is the word, not one or two.

q: The genetic code is _____, meaning it reads as a series of three-letter codons without spaces or overlap.
e: The genetic code is continuous, meaning it reads as a series of three-letter codons without spaces or overlap. The blank is continuous. Not redundant or universal.

q: A shift of _____ nucleotides in either direction can alter the codon groupings and result in an incorrect sequence.
e: A shift of one or two nucleotides in either direction can alter the codon groupings and result in an incorrect sequence. So we write one or two. Leave three or four and five or six out.

q: The genetic code is nearly _____, meaning almost all organisms build proteins with the same genetic code.
e: The genetic code is nearly universal, meaning almost all organisms build proteins with the same genetic code. The blank is universal. Not redundant or continuous.

q: The universality of the genetic code means that a codon in the fruit fly codes for the _____ amino acid as in a human.
e: The universality of the genetic code means that a codon in the fruit fly codes for the same amino acid as in a human. The blank is same. Not different or opposite.

q: The universality of the genetic code has important implications for gene technology, such as _____.
e: The universality of the genetic code has important implications for gene technology, such as mutation. So we write mutation. Leave replication and cloning out.

q: A gene taken from one organism and inserted into another kind of organism will produce the _____ protein.
e: A gene taken from one organism and inserted into another kind of organism will produce the mutated protein. The blank is mutated. Not different or same.

q: Which of the following is a start codon that also codes for the amino acid methionine?
e: The answer is AUG. AUG is a start codon and it also codes for the amino acid methionine. Not UAA or UAG.

q: Which of the following amino acids is coded by the start codon AUG?
e: The answer is methionine. AUG is a start codon. Not alanine or valine.

q: UAA, UAG, and UGA are _____ codons that serve as stop signals to end protein synthesis.
e: UAA, UAG, and UGA are sense codons that serve as stop signals to end protein synthesis. Sense is the word, not start or terminator.
